name: Docker Compose
description: Protects against destructive Docker Compose operations like \ 'down -v' which removes volumes

destructive_patterns.name: down-volumes
destructive_patterns.description: docker-compose down -v removes volumes and their data permanently.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The -v/--volumes flag causes docker-compose down to remove named volumes declared \ in the volumes section of the Compose file, as well as anonymous volumes attached \ to containers. This permanently destroys:

\ - Database data (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB volumes) \ - User uploads and application state \ - Any persistent configuration stored in volumes

\ Safer alternatives: \ - docker-compose down: Stops and removes containers without touching volumes \ - docker-compose stop: Stops containers, preserving everything \ - docker volume ls: List volumes before removal

destructive_patterns.name: down-rmi-all
destructive_patterns.description: docker-compose down --rmi all removes all images used by services.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The --rmi all flag removes all images used by services in the Compose file. \ This forces re-downloading or rebuilding images on next 'up':

\ - Base images must be pulled again (bandwidth, time) \ - Custom built images need rebuilding \ - Layers not in registry are lost

\ Safer alternatives: \ - docker-compose down: Preserves images for faster restarts \ - docker-compose down --rmi local: Only removes images without custom tag \ - docker image ls: Review images before removal

destructive_patterns.name: rm-volumes
destructive_patterns.description: docker-compose rm -v removes volumes attached to containers.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The -v flag with docker-compose rm removes anonymous volumes attached to the \ containers being removed. This can cause data loss if volumes contain:

\ - Application state or session data \ - Cached data that takes time to rebuild \ - Temporary but important processing results

\ Safer alternatives: \ - docker-compose rm: Removes containers without volumes \ - docker-compose stop: Stops without removing anything \ - docker volume ls: Check what volumes exist

destructive_patterns.name: rm-force
destructive_patterns.description: docker-compose rm -f forcibly removes containers without confirmation.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The -f/--force flag removes containers without asking for confirmation. While \ this doesn't directly cause data loss, it can be risky:

\ - Running containers are stopped abruptly (SIGKILL) \ - No graceful shutdown for applications \ - In-flight requests or transactions may be lost

\ Safer alternatives: \ - docker-compose stop: Graceful shutdown first \ - docker-compose rm: Asks for confirmation \ - docker-compose ps: Check container status first
